messages:
mike: Heads up — after enabling FP8 KV-cache + dynamic kernel routing on Mixtral we saw a 12% p95 latency regression in production for chat workloads. Not a throughput drop, latencies shifted right.

sara: ugh. any idea which part routes to the slow kernel?

mike: profiler attached (snippet):
```
NVTX: request -> batch_select -> kv_cache_lookup(fp8) -> dequantize -> matmul(fallback_fp16) -> kv_write
CPU: kernel_selector chose `fp8_dequant_then_fp16_gemm` path with memcpy spikes
QPS steady, but tail up.
```

alexa: two quick suspects: batching wait heuristics increasing queuing for small chat tokens, or RoPE scaling path triggering conversion for certain seq-lens. Did the regression show seq-len dependence?

mike: yes, > 512 tokens sessions show the worst. Short sessions unaffected. Also seen more memcpy in timeline around kv dequant.

devon: that smells like kernel-selection fallback because the fast FP8 GEMM kernel only supports head_dim multiples of 64. Mixtral head_dim=80/96? which variant are we using?

mike: Mixtral-7B variant is head_dim=128 for some layers and 96 for others (we use fused layout). Runtime ended up splitting layers and using generic gemm for the 96-head layers.

alexa: batching heuristics: current max_wait_ms=6 and hard_max_batch=32. For tails >512 we get long KV cache touch and dequant cost per element. Try lowering max_wait_ms to 2 for those model routes, or implement dynamic batch cutoff by seq_len.

rui: also consider two-tier KV cache: keep hot prefixes in FP16 to avoid dequant on hot path, cold entries in FP8/quantized. Eviction policy = LRU+age threshold. That reduces dequant ops on hot path.

mike: good idea. Preliminary mem calc: FP16 KV for 1M tokens ~ 32GB more, but if we keep just last-100k per worker it's ~3.2GB. Worth it.

devon: another angle: RoPE scaling. For Llama-like layers we do compute scaled RoPE in FP32 then cast; for some mixtral layers new code computed RoPE in FP16 causing extra casts when combining with FP8 KV. Reverting RoPE to fp32 for scaling ops cut a bunch of copies in my local.

perf-bot: CI perf-run 2026-03-18T09:02 (run 4021) — baseline vs fp8-kvcache-branch: p50 +0.2%, p95 +11.7%, p99 +14.4%, avg memcpy time +27ms. Full artifacts: https://ci.internal/runs/4021

sara: thanks bot. mike — can you run a canary with: (1) FP8 KV for cold tier + FP16 hot tier, (2) dynamic batch cutoff by seq_len, (3) block kernel_selector for the fallback path so it forces a compatible kernel where possible? We need 24h Canary.

mike: starting canary now. will enable feature flags: `kvcache.tier_hot_format=fp16`, `batch.dynamic_by_seq=true`, `kernel_selector.disable_generic_fallback=true` for route mixtral-chat-prod-canary.

alexa: add metric: percent dequant time per request and memcpy spikes in per-token trace. Also add a roll-back alert if p95 > baseline * 1.08.

rui: i can prototype async eviction that compacts FP8 cold entries to int8 on overflow to save RAM. If we keep metadata to map tiers it should be cheap to implement.

devon: small test idea: patch kernel selector to prefer splitting a mixed-head layer into two GEMMs that hit the fast kernel vs using the generic kernel. Might be faster even with extra ops. Can benchmark today.

mike: plan of record: run canary with changes above, collect traces, then decide between hot-FP16 vs kernel-splitting. will post results in ~8-12h. thanks all :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Canary started: canary-1769998887-1, targets=20% traffic, sampling=1%. Monitoring dashboards: https://grafana.internal/d/kv-cache-canary

sara: awesome. keep this thread for updates. small replies only plz.
